| MLX device scope `device("mlx") { }` | Engram MLX demo | opt-in lab scale |

## Awkward but apparently expressible

| Capability | Why awkward | Downstream experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Sparse expert dispatch | no scatter-add or batched gather across experts on the tape; per-token loops in the interpreter | dense-masked training plus forward-only sparse dispatch with parity assertion |
| Top-k gate on the tape | `argtop_k` is not differentiable; gate must be softmax over masked logits | masked-softmax probe in step 2 |

| Quantized weights | no integer dtype; INT8/INT4 are integer-valued f64 arrays plus packed byte files | byte accounting from packed files, not from in-memory arrays |
| Multiple observations per step and non-numeric annotations | numeric-only frames; no typed envelope | stable slash names plus lesson text, as in the peer |
| Wall-clock speed | interpreter timing is machine-dependent | counted costs are primary; `clock_ms()` reported with binary version |

   of models and raw params in one call.
2. Gradient flow through the same model applied `R` times inside `repeat`
   with an accumulated loss.
3. Differentiability of `gather_rows` and of `softmax` over masked logits.
4. Existence and signature of a KL-divergence builtin; otherwise KL is
   written from `softmax` and `log`.
5. Interpreter cost of a per-token routing loop at `T` 16, `E` 8, measured
   with `clock_ms()`.
6. Whether `emit_frame` inside `train { }` streams every step or only the
   final one on the connect path.

A confirmed blocker must add a minimal `.mlpl` reproducer, the configured
binary version, expected signature and semantics, positive/negative/boundary
acceptance cases, affected lessons, and an explicit currently-unavailable
result. Until then, no `sw-mlpl` change is requested.

# moe-microscope

Building mixture-of-experts models small enough to understand.

`moe-microscope` is an sw-MLPL project that builds a tiny mixture-of-experts
language model, MicroMoE, from scratch and lets a learner look inside every
part of it. The model combines four ideas that normally live at very different
scales: FreeToken-style heterogeneous expert execution (an expert cache that
follows real routing decisions), HRM/TRM-style recursion (one shared block
applied several times instead of many unique layers), DeepSeek-style Engram
conditional memory (hashed n-gram lookup instead of neural memorization), and
ordinary sparse routing over many tiny experts.

Each mechanism is a separate, executable lesson. Every lesson records its own
intermediate values, ships annotated diagrams of each data structure and
transformation, and measures memory, speed, and quality. The learner reads the
MLPL, changes it, reruns it, and watches the numbers and pictures change.

## Summary

The repository progresses through comparable stages rather than starting from
the final architecture:

| Stage | Lesson | What it adds | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | DN01 | dense tiny transformer | the baseline |
| 1 | RC01 | one shared block applied `R` times | does repeated compute replace parameters? |
| 2 | EG01 | Engram n-gram memory, built from scratch | does external memory help? |
| 3-4 | MX01, MX02 | top-1 and top-2 routing over a bank of experts | can experts specialize, and is top-2 worth it? |
| 5-6 | RM01, RE01 | recurrent MoE, then with Engram | does routing change over reasoning time? |
| 7 | KD01 | distillation from an in-repo teacher | which distillation term buys what? |
| 8 | QZ01 | INT8 then INT4 experts | what quality is lost, how many more experts fit? |
| 9 | XC01 | capacity-limited LRU expert cache | what does cache size do to hits, bytes, speed? |
| 10 | HY01 | CPU/NPU hybrid with the q-star split | can FreeToken-style scheduling help? |
| 11 | PK01 | packed TinyMoE file and a 256 MB budget | can the whole thing survive an embedded budget? |

The model works in a constrained mixture where value is measurable per task:
small-integer arithmetic, sequence transformations, tiny MLPL expressions
checked against the interpreter itself, and short templated prose. Experts are
distilled at four levels, token distributions from a teacher, a router warm
start from task tags, low-rank expert deltas fitted to a dense teacher, and
deep supervision across recurrences, each measured alone against the baseline.
The [delivery plan](docs/plan.md) explains both choices in detail.

The microscope scale (CPU, seconds, tens of thousands of parameters) is the
acceptance scale for every lesson. The same source runs at a lab scale under
`device("mlx") { }`. The 256 MB, 0.5 TOPS device is an inference target for
the packed file, not a training target.

## What is here

```text
docs/plan.md                 Delivery plan, sagas, the distillation and domain answers
docs/sagas.md                Saga queue (active and future)
docs/architecture.md         Ownership, layering, the model under the lens
docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md     Capability ledger: supported, awkward, to be probed
docs/cross-repo-handoffs.md  Read-only work orders for sibling repositories
docs/results.md              Memory/speed/quality rows, one per lesson run
docs/research.txt            The original design discussion
lib/  demos/  tests/         MLPL model code, lessons, and native mlplunit tests
fixtures/  assets/previews/  Bounded fixtures and committed diagrams
catalog/                     Machine-readable lesson inventory
scripts/  justfile           Thin gate and tool-selection scripts
```

Lesson code lands saga by saga; see [`docs/sagas.md`](docs/sagas.md) for what
is active.

## Build and run

Prerequisites:

- the adjacent `../sw-mlpl` checkout built in release mode
  (`target/release/mlpl-repl`), or an absolute `MLPL` override;
- `mlplunit` on `PATH`, an absolute `MLPLUNIT` override, or the adjacent
  `../../softwarewrighter/mlplunit/bin/mlplunit` checkout;
- [`just`](https://github.com/casey/just);
- `agentrail` for the development process.

The scripts only select existing tools; they never install or overwrite them.

```sh

just check           # the complete pre-commit gate
just tests           # native mlplunit tests (arguments filter paths or tags)
just mlpl-style      # canonical formatting and docstring checks
```

`just check` currently validates repository structure, documentation links,
peer-identical license files, the generated Agentrail briefing, and MLPL style.
Each lesson extends the gate with its own demo run, preview freshness check,
recording check, and catalog check.

code in this effort subject to `sw-checklist`.

## Development process

Work is divided into durable Agentrail steps. In each fresh session run
`agentrail next`, then `agentrail begin`; implement only that step; run focused
tests and `just check`; commit source and `.agentrail/` metadata by name; push
`main`; and only then run `agentrail complete`. [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) holds
the full repository protocol and `CLAUDE.md` links to it.

## Copyright and license

Copyright (c) 2026 Michael A Wright. See [COPYRIGHT](COPYRIGHT).

Distributed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

This repository uses Agentrail sagas and `AGENTS.md` as its single instruction
source. `CLAUDE.md` is a relative symbolic link to `AGENTS.md`; never replace
it with duplicated content or edit it independently.

## Repository policy

- Work directly on `main`; do not create feature branches or pull requests.
  This project-specific rule overrides the generated branch-handoff guidance
  above. Publication is named-file `git add`, a detailed `git commit`, and
  `git push origin main`. Never force-push or bypass hooks.
- Follow `agentrail next`, `agentrail begin`, work, test, commit, push,
  `agentrail complete`, then stop. Never hand-edit Agentrail-managed state.
- Commit source, documentation, tests, fixtures, and durable `.agentrail/`
  state together before completing a step. Stage named files, never broad
  worktree sweeps.
- Treat every sibling repository as read-only. Record separately actionable
  work in `docs/cross-repo-handoffs.md`; never change a sibling from here.
- Never install or overwrite stable user tools. Prefer explicit absolute tool
  overrides (`MLPL`, `MLPLUNIT`), then `PATH`, then the documented adjacent
  development checkouts selected by `scripts/select-*`.

## MoE microscope contract

- This is primarily an sw-MLPL project. MLPL owns the model (MicroMoE), the
  training loops, data generators, evaluation oracles, quantizers, packed-file
  reader/writer, expert-cache simulator, hybrid scheduler, lesson order,
  observation names, and lesson text. Hosts own only generic rendering,
  transport, retention, playback, and interaction.
- Every lesson satisfies the visual and measurement contract in
  `docs/plan.md`: an annotated what/why/how diagram for each data structure
  and transformation, a step strip for the run, and recorded memory, speed,
  and quality measurements written to the catalog and `docs/results.md`.
  Diagrams are derived from the same recorded values the tests assert on.
- Training uses the dense-masked MoE formulation; inference uses sparse
  dispatch. Every lesson that introduces a sparse path asserts parity with
  the dense-masked path on the same fixture.
- Keep lessons deterministic, bounded, standalone, and honest about which
  work runs in MLPL, in a builtin, or in a simulator. State the microscope
  scale configuration used for acceptance; lab scale under `device("mlx")` is
  opt-in.
- Use `emit_frame` as the low-level observation primitive and return observed
  values unchanged. Do not request new upstream syntax or builtins until an
  executable probe in `docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md` demonstrates a blocking gap.
- Promote helpers to `../demo-mlpl-libraries` only after three unrelated
  lessons prove a stable, domain-neutral API. Generic viewer work belongs in
  `../demo-extensions`; no host may contain router, cache, or Engram
  semantics.

## Testing and completion gate

- Use test-driven development for executable behavior. MLPL behavior requires
  native mlplunit tests with the root `mlplunit.conf`, `tests/test_*.mlpl`,
  `@test` registration, shared assertions, and one `u:run_registered_tests()`
  call per suite.
- Every tracked `.mlpl` file starts with a module-purpose comment; every
  user-defined function has a first-expression docstring; canonical formatting
  with `../sw-mlpl/scripts/mlpl-fmt.sh` is mandatory. Run
  `scripts/check-mlpl-style` before every commit and push.
- Use the root `justfile` as the entry point and keep recipes thin. Portable
  behavior lives in `scripts/`; do not add a Makefile.
- Before every commit and push, run `just check`. The gate grows with each
  lesson: demo run, preview freshness, recording check, catalog check, and
  results-table check.
- `sw-checklist` applies only to Rust code. If a Rust/Yew/WASM live demo is
  ever built (here under `crates/` or in `../demo-extensions`), that Rust
  code, and only that code, must pass `sw-checklist`.
- Update README, architecture, catalog, capability ledger, handoffs, results
  table, and acceptance evidence in the same step as affected behavior.
- Inspect `.gitignore` and `git status --short`, stage named paths, commit on
  `main`, push with `git push origin main`, and verify success before
  reporting completion.
- Run `agentrail complete` only after the implementation commit, successful
  gate, and push. If completion changes durable metadata, commit and push
  those exact files separately, then make no further source changes.
- At the end of every Agentrail step, summarize what was completed, checks
  run, commit/push status, what the next step will deliver, and explicit
  blockers or limitations (`none` when there are none).

Planning references: `docs/research.txt`, `docs/plan.md`, `docs/sagas.md`,
`docs/architecture.md`, `docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md`,
`docs/cross-repo-handoffs.md`, and `docs/results.md`.
EOF
} > AGENTS.new && mv AGENTS.new AGENTS.md && agentrail instructions status && echo "--- add steps ---" && agentrail add --slug foundation-contract --role meta --task-type repository-foundation --prompt "Establish this repository foundation only: install the generated Agentrail briefing and project rules in AGENTS.md with CLAUDE.md as a symlink; add peer-identical COPYRIGHT and LICENSE; complete README.md with intro, summary, build instructions, copyright and license; write docs/plan.md (including the distillation and domain answers and the visual/measurement contract), docs/sagas.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md, docs/cross-repo-handoffs.md, and docs/results.md; add a documentation-only just check gate with tool-selection scripts. Do not add MLPL lesson implementations and do not modify sibling repositories. Commit and push docs before implementation begins." && agentrail add --slug capability-probes --role production --task-type mlpl-probe --prompt "Write native mlplunit probes for the items listed under 'To be probed' in docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md: adam over a mixed list of models and params; gradient flow through the same model applied R times inside repeat; differentiability of gather_rows and of softmax over masked logits as a top-k gate; existence/signature of a KL-divergence builtin (else write KL from softmax and log); per-token routing loop cost at T=16, E=8 measured with clock_ms; emit_frame behavior inside train blocks. Record each result as supported, awkward, or blocked with evidence in the ledger. Add the smallest observation facade over emit_frame in lib/ with tests. Extend just check with run-tests. Do not implement lessons yet." && agentrail add --slug synthetic-domain-and-evaluation --role production --task-type mlpl-lesson --prompt "Implement deterministic seeded generators in lib/ for the four task families (small-integer arithmetic, sequence transformations, tiny MLPL expressions checked against the interpreter, short templated prose) with task tags, fixed mixture ratios as a fixture, and train/validation splits over a restricted byte-level alphabet. Implement exact-match oracles and an evaluation harness reporting per-task accuracy, and a results-table writer that appends a row to docs/results.md with the fixed columns. Produce annotated what/why/how diagrams (committed SVG) for the token window, tag, and split data structures. Native mlplunit tests first; extend just check." && agentrail add --slug dense-baseline-lesson --role production --task-type mlpl-lesson --prompt "Implement DN01, the dense tiny transformer baseline at microscope scale (vocabulary 64-96, d_model 16-32, one block, T 8-16), as a readable standalone lesson in demos/ built from lib/ modules. Record observations with stable slash names via the facade, generate the annotated step strip and data-structure/transformation diagrams from the recorded values, measure the memory/speed/quality triple (param_count, active params per token, ms per step and per token via clock_ms, validation loss, perplexity, per-task exact-match accuracy), append the first results row, add a catalog entry, and freshness-check the preview SVG in just check. Tests first." && agentrail add --slug in-repo-teacher-fixture --role production --task-type mlpl-fixture --prompt "Train the larger in-repo dense teacher (same DN01 source at a larger configuration, e.g. d_model 64, two blocks) once with a fixed seed, export its next-token probability distributions over the training split as a bounded fixture with a documented schema (fixtures/teacher/), record the teacher's own triple and results row, and add a hash and size check for the fixture to just check. Document the fixture schema so the external-teacher export in Saga 4 can produce the same shape. Complete the saga with --done and summarize Saga 2 readiness." && agentrail status

# MoE microscope delivery plan

## Outcome

Build a tiny mixture-of-experts language model from scratch in sw-MLPL, one
mechanism at a time, so that a learner can look inside every part of it:
tokens, Engram lookup, recurrent state, router, expert selection, expert cache,
and CPU/NPU scheduling. Every stage is an executable MLPL lesson that records
its own intermediate values, ships an annotated diagram of what happened, and
reports three measurements: memory, speed, and quality.

The model under the lens is called MicroMoE. The repository is the microscope.
The microscope compares MicroMoE against dense, recurrent, Engram, quantized,
cached, and hybrid-execution variants; it is not defined by one architecture.

This is primarily an sw-MLPL project. MLPL owns the model, the training loops,
the data generators, the evaluation, the systems simulators, and the lesson
text. Visual hosts render recorded observations. A Rust/Yew/WASM live demo is
an optional later layer; only that Rust code is subject to `sw-checklist`.

The source discussion is retained in [`research.txt`](research.txt).

### How will we distill the experts?

Engram, and recursion are all initialized fresh in MLPL, and part of the
training signal comes from a more capable teacher. Nothing is pruned or copied

=== PLAN ===
# MoE microscope delivery plan

## Outcome

Build a tiny mixture-of-experts language model from scratch in sw-MLPL, one
mechanism at a time, so that a learner can look inside every part of it:
tokens, Engram lookup, recurrent state, router, expert selection, expert cache,
and CPU/NPU scheduling. Every stage is an executable MLPL lesson that records
its own intermediate values, ships an annotated diagram of what happened, and
reports three measurements: memory, speed, and quality.

The model under the lens is called MicroMoE. The repository is the microscope.
The microscope compares MicroMoE against dense, recurrent, Engram, quantized,
cached, and hybrid-execution variants; it is not defined by one architecture.

This is primarily an sw-MLPL project. MLPL owns the model, the training loops,
the data generators, the evaluation, the systems simulators, and the lesson
text. Visual hosts render recorded observations. A Rust/Yew/WASM live demo is
an optional later layer; only that Rust code is subject to `sw-checklist`.

The source discussion is retained in [`research.txt`](research.txt).

## Two questions answered up front

### How will we distill the experts?

"Distilled from scratch" means: the tokenizer, architecture, router, experts,
Engram, and recursion are all initialized fresh in MLPL, and part of the
training signal comes from a more capable teacher. Nothing is pruned or copied

  ✗ Invalid: Unicode characters, emojis, accents, box-drawing symbols

  Not auto-fixable: Emojis (except common ones), unprintable control characters

content.text:
The foundation is complete, committed, and pushed. The saga is set up and step one is closed out per the Agentrail protocol, so implementation starts in the next session with `agentrail next`.

**What landed** (commits `8775d0e` and `b256432` on `main`, pushed):

- `AGENTS.md` with the generated Agentrail briefing plus project rules, and `CLAUDE.md` as a relative symlink, matching demo-ml-utils and demo-mlpl-libraries.
- `COPYRIGHT` and `LICENSE` byte-identical to the peers. The gate checks this with `cmp` against demo-mlpl-libraries.
- `README.md` with intro, summary table of the eleven stages, build instructions, development process, and license.
- `docs/plan.md` with seven sagas, the two-scale MicroMoE configuration, and a hard per-lesson contract: annotated what/why/how diagrams for every data structure and transformation, a step strip per run, and recorded memory, speed, and quality. Also `docs/sagas.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md`, `docs/cross-repo-handoffs.md`, and `docs/results.md`.
- A documentation-only `just check` gate and tool-selection scripts. `sw-checklist` is scoped to Rust only, if a Yew/WASM demo is ever built.
- Agentrail saga `moe-microscope-foundation` with five steps. Step 1 is complete. Next up: capability probes, synthetic domain and evaluation, DN01 dense baseline, in-repo teacher fixture.

**Your two questions, as answered in the plan:**

Distillation happens at four levels, each measured alone against the dense baseline. Token-level KD from a teacher's next-token distributions, stored as a bounded fixture. A router warm start from task tags for the early part of training, then released to see whether specialization survives. Expert-level distillation where each expert is a low-rank delta over a shared FFN, fitted to the dense teacher's activations on the positions routed to it. Deep supervision across recurrences, TRM-style. The default teacher is a larger dense MLPL model trained in-repo, so everything stays offline and inspectable. An external 1B to 7B local teacher is an opt-in gated export through the demo-ml-utils path with the same fixture schema.

The domain is a constrained mixture scored by exact match: small-integer arithmetic, sequence transformations, tiny MLPL expressions checked against the interpreter itself, and a small share of templated prose for the Engram to memorize. The value demonstration is a pocket helper that answers those prompts from a packed file of a few hundred kilobytes while the microscope shows which experts fired, which Engram rows were read, and how many bytes crossed the simulated cache.

**Two things worth knowing:**

- sw-mlpl already ships `engram`, `apply_engram`, `ngram_hash`, and `engram_stats`, plus KV-cached generation. The plan builds Engram from scratch first and checks parity against the builtin rather than skipping the lesson.
- Six capabilities need executable probes before the MoE lessons, notably multi-model `adam` in one call and gradients through a block applied `R` times inside `repeat`. They are listed in the capability ledger and are the whole of step 2.

content.text:
Short answer: yes, the plan is implementable at microscope scale with existing sw-MLPL features, and the probes already produced four concrete dogfooding findings for the sw-mlpl repo. The evidence below comes from running probe scripts against the adjacent `mlpl-repl 0.22.0`, not from the reference alone.

**What works today, measured**

| Mechanism | Probe result | Plan consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Dense-masked MoE, `adam` over `[expert0, expert1, router_param]` | experts train, loss 7.27 to 0.44; router trains with a Switch-style gate (moved 3.47) | core of Saga 2 is buildable now |
| Recurrence as nested `apply(blk, apply(blk, apply(blk, x)))` | trains, loss 3.39 to 0.99 | Saga 3 recurrence works |
| Engram builtins (`ngram_hash`, `engram`, `apply_engram`, `engram_stats`) | exact no-op at init, stats and `param_count` 1296 as documented | the pragmatic Engram is a builtin call |
| Packed INT8 bytes with bounded `read_bytes(path, 4, 4)` | round trip exact | packed TinyMoE file and cache simulator need nothing new |
| `emit_frame` identity, `argtop_k`, `for row in`, `clock_ms` | as documented; 16-token routing loop cost 0.17 ms | observation, dispatch, and timing are covered |

**Dogfooding findings to report upstream** (each with a reproducer already in my scratchpad):

1. `softmax` arity differs between eager and tape evaluation. Eager requires `softmax(x, axis)`; inside `grad`/`adam` it requires `softmax(x)`. The same loss expression cannot be written once and reused for both evaluation and training. This is a real bug or documentation gap.
2. User-defined functions are rejected inside `grad`/`adam` ("function 'u:moe' not supported inside grad()"). Loss expressions must be written inline, which fights the readable-lesson goal. This is the most important finding for a language that wants to express models as auditable source.
3. `chain(blk, blk, blk)` does not implement weight sharing. `param_count` triple-counts, and `adam` fails with "not a tracked parameter". Nested `apply` is the working spelling.
4. `gather_rows` is not differentiable, and there is no `kl_divergence` builtin. KL is a one-line composition of `softmax` and `log`, so that one is a convenience gap rather than a blocker.

None of these blocks Saga 1 or 2. Each becomes a ledger entry with a reproducer, and the first two are strong candidates for a separately authorized sw-mlpl change.

**Builtin versus from-scratch, per your preference**

- Engram: show both. The from-scratch version (`ngram_hash` + `gather_rows` + hand-written projection and gate) is forward-only because `gather_rows` is not on the tape, so it teaches addressing and gating and then hands training to the `engram` builtin. That split is honest and educational.
- Attention, embedding, cross-entropy, BPE, KV cache, `perplexity`: use the builtins. No educational reason to rewrite them here.
- Router, top-k, dispatch, combine, load balance, expert cache, q-star scheduler: no builtin exists, so these are the from-scratch lessons and the whole point of the repo.
- Quantization: MLPL has no quantize builtin. The plan already reuses the INT8/Q4 arithmetic proven in demo-ml-utils by handoff to demo-mlpl-libraries rather than rewriting it.

**Plan revisions your three messages imply**

- Move the visualization host from "optional later" to a first-class dogfooding track: each lesson from DN01 onward emits a recording that the existing demo-extensions Yew microscope must render, and the interactive live demo uses the MLPL web framework there. Saga 7 becomes a per-saga step, not a tail.
- Add a step 002 deliverable: file the four findings above in the ledger with reproducers and a short `docs/sw-mlpl-findings.md` written as an upstream work order.
- Record the "prefer builtins, show both where educational" rule in `AGENTS.md` and mark each lesson in the catalog as builtin, from-scratch, or both.

I have not changed the repo, since step 001 is closed and you asked a question. Say the word and I'll open the next Agentrail step and apply these revisions as its first commit.

# sw-mlpl dogfooding findings (from ../moe-microscope)

Status: RESOLVED (audit trail). Findings surfaced by the moe-microscope
repo agent probing mlpl-repl 0.22.0 while building the MoE educational
visualization demo (dogfooding sw-mlpl + demo-extensions, not just proving a
model trains). All four were addressed in the `moe-microscope-findings` saga;
each finding below keeps its original reproducer and carries a RESOLVED line
with the fixing commit. Reproduced against 0.22.0; fixes verified in the
rebuilt release binary.

Resolution summary:

| Finding | Severity | Resolution | Commit |
|---------|----------|------------|--------|
| F1 softmax arity | HIGH | `softmax(x)` defaults to the last axis eagerly, matching the tape | `ae7ec747` |
| F2 user fns in grad | HIGH | `u:` calls are inlined onto the grad tape | `41faf626` |
| F3 chain sharing | MEDIUM | documented: chain copies blocks; reuse one block to share | `b28fdf45` |
| F4 gather_rows / KL | LOW | `gather_rows` differentiable (scatter-add); KL documented as a composition | `e1d693af` |

## F1 -- softmax arity differs between eager and tape (HIGH)

Eager evaluation requires an axis; inside `grad`/`adam` (tape) it takes one
argument. The same loss expression cannot be written once and reused for both
evaluation and training.

```
softmax([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])       # error: softmax: expected 2 args, got 1
softmax([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], 0)    # ok -> 0.090..., 0.244..., 0.665...
```
(The moe agent reports the tape path requires the 1-arg form.)

Proposed fix: accept an OPTIONAL axis in both eager and tape (default the last
axis), so `softmax(x)` and `softmax(x, axis)` mean the same in both contexts.
Real bug or at least a doc gap; pick one arity and honor it everywhere.

RESOLVED (`ae7ec747`): eager `softmax(x)` now defaults to the last axis, so a
one-argument softmax means the same thing in evaluation and inside
`grad`/`adam`. `softmax(x, axis)` is unchanged.

## F2 -- user-defined functions rejected inside grad/adam (HIGH; most important)

A `def u:...` cannot be called inside `grad`/`adam`; the loss must be written
inline. This fights the whole point of a language that expresses models as
auditable, reusable source.

```
def u:moe(x) { ... }
grad(u:moe(w), w)   # error: grad: 'u:moe' not supported inside grad()
```
(A minimal `grad(u:sq(w), w)` probe here surfaced the adjacent
"'w' is not a tracked parameter" wall; the moe agent's scratchpad has the
`u:moe` reproducer.)

Proposed fix: trace through user-function calls inside `grad` (inline/expand
the body onto the tape), so a loss defined as `def u:loss(...)` trains.

RESOLVED (`41faf626`): a `u:` call reached inside `grad`/`adam`/`train` is
inlined onto the same reverse-mode tape -- its parameters bind to the traced
arguments and its body is walked statement-by-statement, so it differentiates
exactly as the inline expression. A global param the body references stays
differentiable; a depth guard turns runaway recursion into an error.

## F3 -- chain(blk, blk, blk) does not share weights (MEDIUM; workaround exists)

`chain` triple-counts `param_count` and `adam` fails with "not a tracked
parameter". Nested `apply(blk, apply(blk, apply(blk, x)))` IS the working
spelling for weight-shared recurrence.

Proposed fix: either make `chain` share the block's weights (single tracked
parameter set) or document clearly that `chain` does NOT share and nested
`apply` is the recurrence/weight-sharing spelling.

RESOLVED (`b28fdf45`): documented (by design, chain composes independent
blocks). lang-reference + glossary now state each chain argument is an
independent block whose params are summed; weight sharing / recurrence is
spelled by reusing one block via nested `apply` (or, per F2, a user function),
where the tape accumulates gradient across every use. Pinned by two tests in
`model_dsl_tests` (3x param count; gradient accumulation on reuse).

## F4 -- gather_rows not differentiable; no kl_divergence (LOW; convenience)

`gather_rows` is not on the autograd tape (so a from-scratch Engram addressing
lesson is forward-only). `kl_divergence` is absent:

```
kl_divergence([0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5])   # error: unknown function: kl_divergence
```
KL is a one-line composition of `softmax` and `log`, so this is a convenience
gap, not a blocker.

Proposed fix: add a `gather_rows` backward (scatter-add, like `windows`); add a
`kl_divergence` builtin OR document the composition.

RESOLVED (`e1d693af`): `gather_rows` is now differentiable wrt the table inside
`grad` -- the addressed rows are gathered by a one-hot selection matmul whose
backward is an exact scatter-ADD into the addressed rows (duplicates
accumulate, unaddressed rows stay zero), so a from-scratch addressing /
embedding table trains. `kl_divergence` needs no builtin: it is a direct
composition of shipped builtins that works both eagerly and through `grad` --
`reduce_add(P * (log(P) - log(Q)))`, gradient `-P / Q`. Documented in
lang-reference (Autograd) and the glossary KL entry.

## Triage (historical; all resolved above)

- F1, F2 were the strong candidates for a dedicated saga -- they blocked
  writing a model as reusable source and reusing one loss expression. F2 was
  the most important for the "models as auditable source" goal.
- F3 was documentation (nested `apply` is the intended spelling).
- F4 was a small additive pair (a scatter-add gather backward + a documented
  KL composition; no new builtin needed).

None blocked the moe-microscope Saga 1 or 2; each was a ledger entry with a
reproducer, now closed.

| F4 gather_rows / KL | LOW | `gather_rows` differentiable (scatter-add); KL documented as a composition | `e1d693af` |

## F1 -- softmax arity differs between eager and tape (HIGH)

Eager evaluation requires an axis; inside `grad`/`adam` (tape) it takes one
argument. The same loss expression cannot be written once and reused for both
evaluation and training.

```
softmax([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])       # error: softmax: expected 2 args, got 1
softmax([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], 0)    # ok -> 0.090..., 0.244..., 0.665...
```
(The moe agent reports the tape path requires the 1-arg form.)

Proposed fix: accept an OPTIONAL axis in both eager and tape (default the last
axis), so `softmax(x)` and `softmax(x, axis)` mean the same in both contexts.
Real bug or at least a doc gap; pick one arity and honor it everywhere.

RESOLVED (`ae7ec747`): eager `softmax(x)` now defaults to the last axis, so a
one-argument softmax means the same thing in evaluation and inside
`grad`/`adam`. `softmax(x, axis)` is unchanged.

## F2 -- user-defined functions rejected inside grad/adam (HIGH; most important)

A `def u:...` cannot be called inside `grad`/`adam`; the loss must be written
inline. This fights the whole point of a language that expresses models as
auditable, reusable source.

```
def u:moe(x) { ... }
grad(u:moe(w), w)   # error: grad: 'u:moe' not supported inside grad()
```
(A minimal `grad(u:sq(w), w)` probe here surfaced the adjacent
"'w' is not a tracked parameter" wall; the moe agent's scratchpad has the
`u:moe` reproducer.)

Proposed fix: trace through user-function calls inside `grad` (inline/expand
the body onto the tape), so a loss defined as `def u:loss(...)` trains.

RESOLVED (`41faf626`): a `u:` call reached inside `grad`/`adam`/`train` is
inlined onto the same reverse-mode tape -- its parameters bind to the traced
arguments and its body is walked statement-by-statement, so it differentiates
exactly as the inline expression. A global param the body references stays
differentiable; a depth guard turns runaway recursion into an error.

## F3 -- chain(blk, blk, blk) does not share weights (MEDIUM; workaround exists)

`chain` triple-counts `param_count` and `adam` fails with "not a tracked
parameter". Nested `apply(blk, apply(blk, apply(blk, x)))` IS the working
spelling for weight-shared recurrence.

Proposed fix: either make `chain` share the block's weights (single tracked
parameter set) or document clearly that `chain` does NOT share and nested
`apply` is the recurrence/weight-sharing spelling.

RESOLVED (`b28fdf45`): documented (by design, chain composes independent
blocks). lang-reference + glossary now state each chain argument is an
independent block whose params are summed; weight sharing / recurrence is
spelled by reusing one block via nested `apply` (or, per F2, a user function),
where the tape accumulates gradient across every use. Pinned by two tests in
`model_dsl_tests` (3x param count; gradient accumulation on reuse).

## F4 -- gather_rows not differentiable; no kl_divergence (LOW; convenience)

`gather_rows` is not on the autograd tape (so a from-scratch Engram addressing
lesson is forward-only). `kl_divergence` is absent:

```
kl_divergence([0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5])   # error: unknown function: kl_divergence
```
KL is a one-line composition of `softmax` and `log`, so this is a convenience
gap, not a blocker.

Proposed fix: add a `gather_rows` backward (scatter-add, like `windows`); add a
`kl_divergence` builtin OR document the composition.

RESOLVED (`e1d693af`): `gather_rows` is now differentiable wrt the table inside
`grad` -- the addressed rows are gathered by a one-hot selection matmul whose
backward is an exact scatter-ADD into the addressed rows (duplicates
accumulate, unaddressed rows stay zero), so a from-scratch addressing /
embedding table trains. `kl_divergence` needs no builtin: it is a direct
composition of shipped builtins that works both eagerly and through `grad` --
`reduce_add(P * (log(P) - log(Q)))`, gradient `-P / Q`. Documented in
lang-reference (Autograd) and the glossary KL entry.

## Triage (historical; all resolved above)

- F1, F2 were the strong candidates for a dedicated saga -- they blocked
  writing a model as reusable source and reusing one loss expression. F2 was
  the most important for the "models as auditable source" goal.
- F3 was documentation (nested `apply` is the intended spelling).
- F4 was a small additive pair (a scatter-add gather backward + a documented
  KL composition; no new builtin needed).

None blocked the moe-microscope Saga 1 or 2; each was a ledger entry with a
reproducer, now closed.

Update docs/sw-mlpl-findings.md marking each finding resolved/documented; relay to the moe-microscope agent; refresh CHANGES + wiki; mark the saga shipped in docs/future-sagas-queue.md. --done.
--- lang-reference autograd note ---
65-cleanly.
66-
67:## The Three Kinds of Name: `name` vs `:name` vs `u:name`
68-
69-One naming design, three deliberate roles:
70-
71-| Form | What it is | Example |
72-| --- | --- | --- |
73-| `name(...)` | CALL a builtin. The bare name is only meaningful applied to arguments. | `disp(G)`, `rotate(x, 1, 0)` |
74-| `:name` | QUOTE a builtin into a first-class VALUE (APL's quoted function). What higher-order builtins consume; typing `:disp` alone shows the reference, not a rendering. Applying the quoted form calls it: `:disp(G)` and `disp(G)` are the same call. `:disp G` (no parens) is NOT a command -- the REPL says so. | `reduce(:add, S, 0)`, `f = :max`, `:disp(G)` |
75:| `u:name` | A USER-DEFINED function. The mandatory `u:` namespace prefix keeps your names from ever colliding with (or shadowing) present or FUTURE builtins -- a new builtin release can never break your workspace. | `def u:life(g) { ... }`, `u:life(G)` |
76-
77-Why the trichotomy: calls and values must look different (so
78-`reduce(add, v)` cannot silently pass a VARIABLE named add where
79-a function was meant), and user space and builtin space must
80-look different (APL workspaces suffered decades of name-clash
81-pain; the `u:` prefix is the cure priced at two characters).
82-The quoting rule covers BOTH spaces: `:name` quotes a builtin
83:and `:u:name` quotes YOUR function -- a first-class reference
84-you can bind, store in record fields, pass, and return. A test

Upstream already fixed the findings. The adjacent sw-mlpl checkout is level with its remote, and a dedicated `moe-microscope-findings` saga ran there today (2026-09-12, 17:54 to 20:13) with binaries rebuilt at 20:12. Its last step, "relay-and-close", is still in progress with an uncommitted `docs/sw-mlpl-findings.md` marking all four resolved. I verified each fix against the rebuilt release binary with the same probes.

| Finding | Upstream resolution | Commit | Verified here |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 softmax arity | eager `softmax(x)` now defaults to the last axis, same as the tape | `ae7ec747` | yes, one loss expression evaluates and trains |
| F2 user functions in grad | `u:` calls are inlined onto the tape | `41faf626` | yes, a `def u:moe` plus `def u:mse` trains the experts and router |
| F3 chain weight sharing | documented as by design; reuse one block via nested `apply` or a user function | `b28fdf45` | yes, nested `apply` inside a user function trains recurrence |
| F4 gather_rows / KL | `gather_rows` has a scatter-add backward; KL documented as a composition, no builtin | `e1d693af` | yes, addressed rows get gradient, unaddressed rows stay zero |

**Two new edges surfaced by the rerun**, both with reproducers in my scratchpad and both with clean workarounds:

- **F5: `one_hot` and `argmax` are rejected inside a traced function.** The router mask cannot be computed inside the loss. Workaround: compute the mask eagerly each training step and pass it in as a constant argument, which is what a Switch-style top-1 gate wants anyway. A stop-gradient treatment of index and mask builtins on the tape would be the upstream fix.
- **F6: `repeat` inside a traced function is rejected** ("expression form not supported inside grad()"). Recurrence depth must be spelled as nested `apply` calls, so `R` is a source-level choice rather than a runtime argument. Workaround: one small user function per depth for the lesson's `R` range.

One documentation note worth relaying: `grad(l, T)` where `l` was assigned eagerly returns all zeros silently, because the variable is a constant on the tape. My first gather probe fell into this. A loud error or a reference note would save the next learner an hour.

The upstream worktree also has unrelated uncommitted files (`dist-release/`, `docs/research4.txt`, `x`) alongside the in-progress relay step. I did not touch it.

Net effect on the plan: nothing in Sagas 1 through 3 is blocked, the "prefer builtins" rule now holds for softmax, user-function losses, and `gather_rows`, and F5, F6, and the silent-zero note are the next ledger entries. They belong in step 002 of our saga, which I have not started since you asked only to check.

# sw-MLPL dogfooding findings

This repository dogfoods sw-MLPL (and, for the visualization host,
`../demo-extensions`). Every gap met while building the microscope is
recorded here with a reproducer, a workaround, the lesson it affects, and its
upstream status. The executable evidence is `tests/test_capability_probes.mlpl`
and `tests/test_observe.mlpl` (native mlplunit) plus the standalone
reproducers under `probes/` that `scripts/run-probes` re-checks on every
`just check`. When an upstream fix lands, the pinned probe fails loudly and
this document is updated in the same step.

Binary under test: `mlpl-repl 0.22.0` from the adjacent `../sw-mlpl`
checkout at `a2aa68a4` (2026-09-12), rebuilt after the upstream
`moe-microscope-findings` saga.

## Resolved upstream (verified here)

| Finding | Upstream resolution | Commit | Local evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 `softmax` arity differed between eager and tape evaluation | `softmax(x)` defaults to the last axis eagerly, matching the tape | `ae7ec747` | probe "softmax takes one argument in eager and tape evaluation" |
| F2 user-defined functions rejected inside `grad`/`adam` | `u:` calls are inlined onto the tape | `41faf626` | probe "adam trains a list of expert models plus a router param through a user function" |
| F3 `chain(blk, blk, blk)` does not share weights | documented as by design; weight sharing is spelled by reusing one block through nested `apply` | `b28fdf45` | probe "one shared block applied R times trains through nested apply" |
| F4 `gather_rows` not differentiable; no `kl_divergence` | scatter-add backward for `gather_rows`; KL documented as `reduce_add(P * (log(P) - log(Q)))` | `e1d693af` | probes "gather_rows scatter-adds gradient" and "KL divergence is a composition" |

## Open, queued upstream as `moe-microscope-followups`

### F5: `one_hot` and `argmax` are rejected inside a traced function

```
grad(reduce_add(softmax(matmul(x, W)) * one_hot(argmax(matmul(x, W), 1), 2)), W)
# error: unsupported: grad: function 'one_hot' not supported inside grad()
```

Reproducer: `probes/f5_one_hot_in_grad.mlpl`. Workaround: compute the top-k
mask eagerly each training step and pass it into the loss as a constant
argument. Affects: every router lesson (MX01 onward). Proposed fix: treat
index and mask builtins (`argmax`, `argtop_k`, `one_hot`, `eq`, `gt`, `lt`)
as stop-gradient constants on the tape.

### F6: `repeat` is rejected inside a traced function

Reproducer: `probes/f6_repeat_in_grad.mlpl` ("expression form not supported
inside grad()"). Workaround: nested `apply` per depth, one user function per
`R` value. Affects: RC01, RM01, RE01. Proposed fix: unroll `repeat N` with a
literal or bound integer `N` onto the tape.

### F7: a model value cannot be a user-function argument

```
def u:apply_twice(b, x0) { "..."; apply(b, apply(b, x0)) }
u:apply_twice(linear(2, 2, 1), [[1, 1]])
# error: unsupported: u:apply_twice: argument 'b' must be an array, Result,
#        string, string list, record, function reference, or partial
```

Reproducer: `probes/f7_model_argument.mlpl`. Workaround: refer to models as
globals inside user functions. Affects: reusable lesson source; every helper
that would take an expert, block, or router as a parameter. Proposed fix:
allow `Value::Model` (and tokenizer, generation state, engram) as user-function
arguments by reference.

### F8: `emit_frame` requires a literal name

```
name = str_concat("probe/", "dynamic")
emit_frame(name, 0, [1, 2, 3])
# error: unsupported: emit_frame: name must be a string literal
```

Reproducer: `probes/f8_emit_frame_name.mlpl`. Consequence: an identity
facade `u:observe(name, step, x)` cannot exist, so `lib/observe.mlpl` provides
only naming helpers and lessons call `emit_frame` with literal names.
Affects: observation facade, any generated or parameterized observation name
(per-expert, per-recurrence, per-cache-slot series). Proposed fix: accept any
string value for the name, or document the literal rule and provide a
`str`-valued form.

### D1: `grad` of a pre-evaluated loss variable is silently zero

```
l = reduce_add(W * W)
grad(l, W)                     # [0, 0]  (l is a constant on the tape)
grad(reduce_add(W * W), W)     # [2, 4]
```

Reproducer: `probes/d1_silent_zero_grad.mlpl`. Proposed fix: a loud error
when the `wrt` leaf does not appear on the tape of the expression.

- `emit_frame` inside `train { }` on the connect path: does every step
  stream, or only the last? Deferred to Saga 1 step 6, which records DN01
  over live SSE against the peer schema.
- `device("mlx") { }` at lab scale for the MoE loss written as user
  functions; deferred until a lesson runs at lab scale.

# sw-MLPL dogfooding findings

This repository dogfoods sw-MLPL (and, for the visualization host,
`../demo-extensions`). Every gap met while building the microscope is
recorded here with a reproducer, a workaround, the lesson it affects, and its
upstream status. The executable evidence is `tests/test_capability_probes.mlpl`
and `tests/test_observe.mlpl` (native mlplunit) plus the standalone
reproducers under `probes/` that `scripts/run-probes` re-checks on every
`just check`. When an upstream fix lands, the pinned probe fails loudly and
this document is updated in the same step.

Binary under test: `mlpl-repl 0.22.0` from the adjacent `../sw-mlpl`
checkout at `a2aa68a4` (2026-09-12), rebuilt after the upstream
`moe-microscope-findings` saga.

## Resolved upstream (verified here)

| Finding | Upstream resolution | Commit | Local evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 `softmax` arity differed between eager and tape evaluation | `softmax(x)` defaults to the last axis eagerly, matching the tape | `ae7ec747` | probe "softmax takes one argument in eager and tape evaluation" |
| F2 user-defined functions rejected inside `grad`/`adam` | `u:` calls are inlined onto the tape | `41faf626` | probe "adam trains a list of expert models plus a router param through a user function" |
| F3 `chain(blk, blk, blk)` does not share weights | documented as by design; weight sharing is spelled by reusing one block through nested `apply` | `b28fdf45` | probe "one shared block applied R times trains through nested apply" |
| F4 `gather_rows` not differentiable; no `kl_divergence` | scatter-add backward for `gather_rows`; KL documented as `reduce_add(P * (log(P) - log(Q)))` | `e1d693af` | probes "gather_rows scatter-adds gradient" and "KL divergence is a composition" |

## Open, queued upstream as `moe-microscope-followups`

### F5: `one_hot` and `argmax` are rejected inside a traced function

```
grad(reduce_add(softmax(matmul(x, W)) * one_hot(argmax(matmul(x, W), 1), 2)), W)
# error: unsupported: grad: function 'one_hot' not supported inside grad()
```

Reproducer: `probes/f5_one_hot_in_grad.mlpl`. Workaround: compute the top-k
mask eagerly each training step and pass it into the loss as a constant
argument. Affects: every router lesson (MX01 onward). Proposed fix: treat
index and mask builtins (`argmax`, `argtop_k`, `one_hot`, `eq`, `gt`, `lt`)
as stop-gradient constants on the tape.

### F6: `repeat` is rejected inside a traced function

Reproducer: `probes/f6_repeat_in_grad.mlpl` ("expression form not supported
inside grad()"). Workaround: nested `apply` per depth, one user function per
`R` value. Affects: RC01, RM01, RE01. Proposed fix: unroll `repeat N` with a
literal or bound integer `N` onto the tape.

### F7: a model value cannot be a user-function argument

```
def u:apply_twice(b, x0) { "..."; apply(b, apply(b, x0)) }
u:apply_twice(linear(2, 2, 1), [[1, 1]])
# error: unsupported: u:apply_twice: argument 'b' must be an array, Result,
#        string, string list, record, function reference, or partial
```

Reproducer: `probes/f7_model_argument.mlpl`. Workaround: refer to models as
globals inside user functions. Affects: reusable lesson source; every helper
that would take an expert, block, or router as a parameter. Proposed fix:
allow `Value::Model` (and tokenizer, generation state, engram) as user-function
arguments by reference.

### F8: `emit_frame` requires a literal name

```
name = str_concat("probe/", "dynamic")
emit_frame(name, 0, [1, 2, 3])
# error: unsupported: emit_frame: name must be a string literal
```

Reproducer: `probes/f8_emit_frame_name.mlpl`. Consequence: an identity
facade `u:observe(name, step, x)` cannot exist, so `lib/observe.mlpl` provides
only naming helpers and lessons call `emit_frame` with literal names.
Affects: observation facade, any generated or parameterized observation name
(per-expert, per-recurrence, per-cache-slot series). Proposed fix: accept any
string value for the name, or document the literal rule and provide a
`str`-valued form.

### D1: `grad` of a pre-evaluated loss variable is silently zero

```
l = reduce_add(W * W)
grad(l, W)                     # [0, 0]  (l is a constant on the tape)
grad(reduce_add(W * W), W)     # [2, 4]
```

Reproducer: `probes/d1_silent_zero_grad.mlpl`. Proposed fix: a loud error
when the `wrt` leaf does not appear on the tape of the expression.

## Still to be probed

- `emit_frame` inside `train { }` on the connect path: does every step
  stream, or only the last? Deferred to Saga 1 step 6, which records DN01
  over live SSE against the peer schema.
- `device("mlx") { }` at lab scale for the MoE loss written as user
  functions; deferred until a lesson runs at lab scale.

This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

The operation is refused if any step that would shift is already `Completed`, since completed steps anchor git-tracked history.

Pass `--after 0` to prepend at position 1 (only works if step 1 is pending).

Cursor semantic (preemption): if the new step lands at or before the current cursor, focus follows the new arrival — the inserted step becomes `current_step` and the previously focused step is pushed to `current_step + 1`. This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

Step 002 is complete, committed, and pushed (`a91bc45`, `56d3c21`). The saga cursor is now on step 003, synthetic domain and evaluation.

**What the probes established** (16 native mlplunit tests plus 5 standalone reproducers, all run by `just check`):

- F1 through F4 are verified fixed against the rebuilt upstream binary. A MoE loss written as `def u:moe` plus `def u:mse` now trains two experts and the router in one `adam` call over a mixed list.
- Four new findings and one note are pinned as expected hard errors, so an upstream fix fails our gate loudly and prompts a doc update:
  - F5: `one_hot`/`argmax` rejected inside `grad`. Workaround: eager mask passed as a constant.
  - F6: `repeat` rejected inside a traced function. Workaround: nested `apply`.
  - F7: a model value cannot be a user-function argument. Workaround: globals.
  - F8: `emit_frame` requires a literal name. Consequence: no forwarding facade; `lib/observe.mlpl` is naming helpers only.
  - D1: `grad` of a pre-evaluated loss variable is silently zero.
- Details, reproducers, and proposed fixes are in `docs/sw-mlpl-findings.md`.

**Plan revisions applied** across plan, sagas, architecture, AGENTS, README, handoffs, and the ledger:

- The host is dogfooded from the first lesson. Every lesson emits a recording, every saga ends with a demo-extensions host step, and the live demo lands on the MLPL web framework after Saga 3. Inserted step 005 `dn01-recording-and-host-handoff` accordingly.
- Builtin first, from scratch only where it teaches, then both forms with a parity check. The catalog will record each lesson as builtin, from-scratch, or both.
- Findings are a first-class deliverable with a reproducer, pinned probe, and work order in the same step.

**On the upstream agent's question:** yes, start `moe-microscope-followups` now. Lead with F5 as proposed, then F8 before F6, because F8 blocks parameterized observation names (per-expert, per-recurrence series) and F6 has a clean unroll workaround. F7 and F8 are new since their scorecard and are already reproduced under `probes/` here.

content.content:
## String Literals

```
"scatter"
"line"
"hello"
```

Double-quoted ASCII strings. Strings are a separate value kind from
arrays and are used as type-name arguments to built-ins like `svg()`.
Strings cannot be combined with numeric operators.

### if / else expression

`if cond { then } else { else }` returns the value of whichever
branch is chosen. The `else` clause is required (no dangling-if).
Both bodies are statement sequences, with the final statement's
value being the branch value -- same convention as `repeat` /
`train` / `for` blocks.

`cond` is truthy when:

- It is a scalar `Number` and not zero (any non-zero value,
  including negatives, NaN, and infinity).
- It is a `Result` and its `ok` field is true (i.e. `Ok(_)`).

Other types (non-scalar arrays, strings, string lists, records,
etc.) raise a runtime error.

```mlpl
flag = 1
x = if flag { 100 } else { 200 }    # x = 100

# Result-as-condition: branches on the Ok / Err discriminant.
name = unwrap_or(env("USER"), "guest")
greeting = if env("USER") { str_concat("hello ", name) } else { "no user" }

cd /Users/mike/github/sw-ml-study/moe-microscope && git add README.md justfile docs/sagas.md docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md lib/domain.mlpl lib/evaluate.mlpl lib/results.mlpl tests/test_domain.mlpl tests/test_evaluate.mlpl tests/test_results.mlpl fixtures/domain/mixture-v0.json demos/domain_microscope.mlpl assets/previews/domain-window.svg assets/previews/domain-tags.svg assets/previews/domain-split.svg catalog/lessons.toml scripts/run-domain-demo scripts/check-catalog scripts/check scripts/check-structure && git rm -q --cached assets/previews/.gitkeep catalog/.gitkeep demos/.gitkeep fixtures/.gitkeep 2>/dev/null; git status --short | grep -vE '^[AMDR]  ' ; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Add the synthetic domain, exact-match evaluation, results writer, and DM01

lib/domain.mlpl: a 52-symbol restricted alphabet where a character's index
is its token id; seeded generators for four task families (small-integer
arithmetic, rev/sort sequence transformations, tiny MLPL expressions whose
answers come from the named builtin, templated prose with a fixed
animal-to-place pattern) each with an exact oracle; the mixture fixture
fixtures/domain/mixture-v0.json (120 examples, window 28, 0.75 train); padded
x/y/mask windows stacked to [N, T]; and a seeded grade_up split.

lib/evaluate.mlpl: exact-match hits and per-family plus overall accuracy.
lib/results.mlpl: the 21 fixed results columns, row formatting, and append.

demos/domain_microscope.mlpl (DM01) emits data/tags, data/window/*, and
data/split/* observations and writes three annotated what/why/how diagrams
(token window, task tags, split) from the same values the tests assert.
scripts/run-domain-demo freshness-checks the committed previews; a write
mode regenerates them. catalog/lessons.toml records DM01 with its
implementation form and memory/speed/quality notes; scripts/check-catalog
validates it. Both run under just check.

Ledger: rank-one gather/reverse/sort, string-list construction, record_get
Result, and include resolution are recorded as awkward with their idioms.

Checks: just check (28 native tests, 5 reproducers, demo freshness, catalog);
sw-markdown-checker; git diff --check; diagrams reviewed at native size.
